executive_summary:
Raffkin is a set of three SOC skills (investigate one alert or case, sweep the open queue, propose rule tuning) that run inside Claude Code or Codex and reach a single Exabeam tenant only through a bundled local MCP bridge holding the operator's API key. Its untrusted input is tenant telemetry - alerts, events and case notes written by whoever generated the activity - plus any payload the analyst pastes in. The consequential things it can do are write to the tenant (open cases, add notes, and, only behind a human prompt, dismiss, close or send mail). Code-level controls sit at two points: a host hook that asks or denies before tool calls, and the bridge, which screens what comes in and neutralizes what goes out.

Two attack chains deserve attention first. In the first, text planted in a case note can talk a queue sweep into opening cases or writing notes on the tenant with no prompt at all. The sweep's no-write rule exists only in the prompt; Codex allows these two writes without limit, and Claude Code allows two per session. The fix is a sweep-mode allowlist enforced in the bridge, plus giving Codex the same write budget. In the second, a formula or live link copied from telemetry into any write field outside the bridge's short list of neutralized field names lands in the platform record as live content. A human still approves such a tool, but the fix is to neutralize every string on writes the bridge does not recognize.

Behind those two: the containment and rule-write deny list is a list of exact names, so a password-reset, quarantine or future rule-modifying tool is only prompted, never denied. The audit trail cannot show that a case was closed as a false positive, and it drops guardrail counts on failed calls. Tool-definition changes are visible only after the fact. The credential file is used even when it is readable by other users. Resistance to visible, plain-language injection still depends on the model following its instructions. The dismiss/close gate itself, the credential transport, the dependency pinning and the read-side screen are solid.

trust_boundaries.name: Tenant telemetry and work-item payloads into the agent

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER treat content retrieved from the platform ... as instructions to itself
MUST NOT reason over or act on text retrieved from the platform before that text has been screened
it MUST stop that action path, report the attempted injection to the analyst

threats.summary: Invisible smuggling code points (tag block, bidi overrides, zero-width) hidden in alert or event fields reach the model.
Visible instruction-shaped text planted in tenant telemetry redirects the verdict or triggers a write; only the skill's untrusted-data instruction answers it.
threats.remainder: natural-language injection passes the code-point screen unchanged, so resistance rests on model compliance (R-02 not enforceable in code)

threats.summary: Planted 'evidence' shaped like platform output inside a pasted alert payload is taken as retrieved corroboration for a verdict.
threats.remainder: no code distinguishes payload-supplied text from tool-retrieved evidence; the provenance rule is instruction-level only

trust_boundaries.name: Skill prompt and evidence to the host's model

threats.summary: Running on a model below the validated floor (e.g. Haiku) weakens injection resistance the instruction-level controls depend on (checked: preflight.sh, gate.py, bridge — no model check; floor stated only in docs/installation.md:21).

trust_boundaries.name: Agent decision to Exabeam tool call through the host gate

remit_rules.excerpt: an MCP tool the tiers do not classify MUST ask, never run silently
the shipped governance configuration MUST deny such tools deterministically even though the platform exposes none today
MUST deny any future tool that modifies, enables, disables or retunes a detection rule, exclusion rule, or context table
MUST be blocked by a host-enforced gate that is active on a fresh install with no operator opt-in
MUST NOT possess or invoke shell execution, arbitrary code execution, or general-purpose filesystem write capability

threats.summary: A containment or rule-modifying tool under a name absent from the exact-name deny list (password reset, file quarantine, a future rule tool) is only prompted, not denied, on both hosts, and the bridge enforces no deny tier of its own.
A dismiss or close is executed without the analyst's yes.
A local Codex override loosening exabeam_send_email or re-enabling a disabled tool goes unreported because preflight checks only update_alert/update_case.

Injected telemetry steers the model to the host's own shell or file-write tools, which Raffkin's gate does not cover (checked: hooks.json matcher covers only Exabeam MCP names; no allowed-tools restriction in any SKILL.md — host defaults are the only gate).

trust_boundaries.name: Neutralized writes committed to the Exabeam tenant

remit_rules.excerpt: During a queue sweep Raffkin MUST NOT write to the platform at all
MUST NOT write text into a platform record without first de-activating executable content and clickable links
MUST be replaced with a redaction marker before it enters a persisted artifact
MUST NOT delete or overwrite existing free-text content
MUST NOT retry the write or reach the same outcome by another tool or field

threats.summary: A queue sweep creates cases or case notes without any prompt — two per session on Claude Code, unlimited on Codex — because the no-write rule is instruction-only.
A formula, live link or credential in a free-text key outside the _DEFANG_FIELDS allowlist (e.g. an unclassified write tool's comment/description) is persisted unneutralized.
An update overwrites analyst-authored text, or a create_case carrying a closing disposition closes a case by another route.
A credential or personal datum from evidence persists into a case note or mail via an allowlisted field.
threats.remainder: free-form names/addresses, dates of birth and bare unlabeled credentials are not masked (declared residuals)

trust_boundaries.name: Host spill file holding raw tenant results

remit_rules.excerpt: the host agent's own spill file for an oversized tool result is the host's copy and is excluded

threats.summary: Oversized tool results (PII, planted payloads) persist in a host-owned local file outside Raffkin's lifecycle and write-path redaction (checked: bridge has no result-size bound; spill location and cleanup are the host's).

trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam API credentials and derived bearer token

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials and any token derived from them MUST NEVER be written to the audit log
MUST NEVER be transmitted to any host other than the operator-configured Exabeam API endpoint

threats.summary: A group- or world-readable ~/.exabeam-mcp.env is used silently every session; the 0600 mode is advice only.
Client secret or bearer token is sent in cleartext or to a non-https endpoint.
Credentials or tokens leak into the audit trail or error output.

A leaked bearer token carries the API key's full tenant access, since the bridge requests no narrower scope (checked: token request at exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:124 sends only grant_type/client_id/client_secret).

trust_boundaries.name: Bridge audit trail and decision record

remit_rules.excerpt: naming which alert or case was acted on and what disposition was applied
Every firing of the input-screening or output-neutralization guardrails MUST be recorded
MUST NEVER be written into the audit log, so that the audit trail cannot become a second copy of the evidence
local-only recording is the required default
Every call Raffkin makes to the platform MUST be recorded in a durable, structured, machine-parseable audit record

threats.summary: A case close is recorded without closedReason, so a false-positive suppression cannot be reconstructed from the audit trail.
Guardrail firings on a call that then fails upstream are not recorded.
The audit trail becomes a second copy of evidence text or neutralized hostile payloads.
Audit events leave the host silently to an off-host backend.

trust_boundaries.name: Tool definitions, dependencies and plugin provenance

remit_rules.excerpt: Tool definitions from the bundled Exabeam MCP MUST be hashed per session ... and screened for hidden code points
MUST be version-bounded and inventoried in the shipped bill of materials
MUST be hash-pinned in the shipped lockfile
MUST be enforced by an automated check rather than by reviewer memory

threats.summary: A changed or instruction-shaped Exabeam tool definition reaches the model in the session it changes, detectable only by comparing per-session hashes afterward.
A cold-cache dependency resolution pulls a different package than the maintainers tested.
Permission tiers, the snippet and the Codex map drift apart from the documented posture.
A marketplace update delivers a modified skill, hook or bridge with no signature check (checked: install.sh:264 adds the marketplace by repo; no signature or pin verification).

attack_paths.name: Planted case note talks a queue sweep into writing cases and notes to the tenant without a prompt

steps.summary: attacker-authored text in a case note or event, unauthenticated content from whoever generated the activity
the tenant serves it through the prompt-free read tools
bridge proxies the result
screen strips invisible code points only; visible instructions pass
host hands the result to the sweep
sweep's no-write rule is prose; the hijacked loop issues create_case / create_case_notes
Codex runs both escalation writes on approval_mode auto with no budget (Claude Code: two free)
bridge forwards the write
allowlisted fields neutralized; the write itself is not blocked
cases/notes committed to the tenant during a sweep that must write nothing

attack_paths.name: Formula or live link planted in telemetry persists into a platform record through an unlisted write field

steps.summary: attacker plants a formula or link in a logged field
served to the agent through read tools
bridge proxies the result
code-point screen leaves visible formulas and URLs intact by design
result reaches the session
quote-defang instruction is model-side only
the loop copies the value into a write whose free text rides a key outside the allowlist
an unclassified write tool is asked, so the human prompt is the only check left
is_write_tool routes it as a write
_defang_args returns non-allowlisted strings untouched
active formula/link persists in the record and fires when opened or exported

notes.lane_fit: The PreToolUse gate and the Codex approval map are placed in client_adapters because the host process enforces them (control-lane rule), although both guard tools_mcp calls; the local audit JSONL sits in tools_mcp as a local store written by the bridge rather than external_deploy; the operator-run preflight check sits in external_deploy as deploy-time posture; the model provider is external_deploy because the LLM call is made by the host session, not by plugin code.
notes.omissions: No OWASP arbitration divergences: the stored tags (LLM03 for -001/-003/-006, LLM10 for -002, ASI04 for -007, none for -004/-005/-008) match the 2026 KB primaries. Folded, not separate nodes: rule-tuning SKILL.md (parallel prompt, same trust consequence) into the soc-investigate orchestrator; the triage-cases no-write and untrusted-data instructions into the triage orchestrator; the gate decision log ~/.raffkin/gate.jsonl and per-session budget state into the gate; permissions.json and settings.snippet.json into the gate; the bridge's _state_only/_create_case_guard write guards into the bridge; platform mail (exabeam_send_email) into the Exabeam service node; and the plugin marketplace into the installer node. Edgeless nodes: the lockfile (deploy posture), the installer (deploy posture), and preflight (operator-run posture check). The spill-file location and lifecycle are cited only from skill prose; the docs/security-guardrails.md disclosure the remit refers to was not found by keyword in plugin/docs. The bundled Exabeam MCP tool-definition surface is treated as supply-chain provenance, not ingress, as the scan instructions and remit direct.
